stance.label: Bearish near term · long term in the bottom zone

headline: Bearish near term, cheap long term: selling and leverage haven't cleared, but valuations sit in past bottom zones; 62K is the line.
summary: Near term, bearish: short-term holders are on day 7 of concentrated loss-taking, yet funding bounced to 6.5%, so leverage and ETF selling have not cleared. Long term, bullish: the Dawn–Dusk Index is in deep night and unrealized profit is at the cycle floor, levels followed by higher prices a year later every time so far. The key is 62K: holding it completes the handover; below it there is little supply until 58K.

watch.label: 200-day average
watch.note: 5 straight closes below; a 12.4% rally would take it back above

overview.lead: The hedge rule fired today, but price did not make a new low: the close at 64,811 was down only 0.8%, and the selling is concentrated in short-term holders taking losses.
points: The day ranged 63,840–65,634 and closed mid-range; volume was 1.3x the 20-day average.
Short-term holders realized 10,793 BTC of loss against 2,107 BTC of profit, a 5-to-1 ratio (CheckOnChain, Nov 16).
Fear & Greed is 10, a 4th day of extreme fear; Polymarket puts a December hike at 96%, up from 77% a week ago.

cycle.lead: Valuation and trend both sit in the bottom zone: Dawn Index heat is 7.7, still Deep night, and the weekly trend score is −0.65 with the trend pointing down.
points: The market stage is still bull, day 39: the 200-day average at 72,865 is still rising, and it takes 30 closes below a falling average to return to bear; only 1 of 6 supporting lights is on (exchange supply).
Relative unrealized profit is 34.4%, a 3rd day under the 35% floor, a level seen since 2012 only near cycle bottoms.
Tidemark's bottom signal is 35.3 with timing at 95.5, short of the 50 bottom-zone line; the test of the June 30 low at 58,525 runs to Dec 19.
Day 406 after this cycle's top, price is down 48.1%; the three prior cycles were all below −75% on the same day.

market.lead: Day 3 of the bottom combo: Sell Pressure Index (SPI) at 100 and momentum at 0.11, deeper than yesterday.
points: The combo has appeared 20 times since 2012, and after the August 2014 and May 2022 cases price still fell another 30–40%, so it does not mark a low.
This leg is down 25.2% over 56 days since Sep 21, already deeper than the −19.4% median of this cycle's 12 down legs; the leg-end line at 73,732 is 13.8% above.

deriv.lead: Leverage did not get flushed: funding bounced from 1.0% to 6.5% in a day, and 75% of accounts are still long.
points: This page's finding: Binance at 6.8% and Hyperliquid at 10.1%, and every venue that went negative over the weekend is positive again; perps saw 81K BTC of net taker selling over 7 days, so sellers and paying longs are both active.

7-day implied vol is 44.2% against 40.5% at 90 days, still inverted by 3.7 points but far calmer than the 16 points on Nov 14; the 25-delta risk reversal is −5.24, so downside protection is still pricier.

Estimated long liquidation bands sit at 61.4–61.9K (4.9% below the close) and 59.5–61.3K, from Coinalyze aggregated open interest plus assumed leverage; within 5% of the close, estimated long and short liquidations are similar, 13K and 15K BTC.
The thickest book is at 64,000 on both sides: $217M bid and $182M ask, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: US-side selling has not stopped: Coinbase spot shows nearly 10K BTC of net taker selling over 7 days, and ETFs are on 7 straight days of outflows.
points: ETFs saw −$185M on Nov 13 and −$2.08B over 20 days (CoinMarketCap); the Nov 16 figure is not out yet.
The Korea premium went 2.99% → 2.33%: Asian premium buying is still there but cooling.
Stablecoins are $287.1B, down $15.6B in 30 days (DefiLlama); USDT trades at $0.9990, and this month's average so far is the lowest in 50 months.
Realized cap 30-day change is −0.28% (CoinMetrics, Nov 15), a 3rd day below zero: less money is coming in than is being sold.

onchain.lead: Price is back in the thickest short-term holder layer at 64–66K, where about 390K BTC changed hands at a loss this week, resetting cost basis near the current price.
points: This page's finding: STH-SOPR is 0.963, the lowest in 282 days; concentrated loss-taking strength is 5.27, day 7.
The share of long-term holders in loss is 41.7%, below this cycle's peak of 45.4%; it would take a drop to an estimated 60,500 to exceed it (CheckOnChain).
LTH-SOPR is 0.860 with a 7-day average of 0.962; long-term holders' 7-day realized loss is $2.05B, against $3.1–3.6B at this cycle's three lows (Bitview).

exit.lead: The exit plan acts today: 5 straight closes below the 200-day average at 72,865, so hedge 20%.
points: There are two ways to buy back: 5 straight closes above 72,865, or the MVRV Z 7-day average under 0.5; it is 0.53 with the daily at 0.37 (CoinMetrics, Nov 15), so the second could land within days.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.438, far from the 0.75 line (111,762); the three top indicators read 13 / 12 / 49, all low.

news.title: Nasdaq fell 1.98% on Monday to 24,639; Strategy dropped 7.4% and Coinbase 6.3%
news.read: BTC fell only 0.8% the same day, so crypto stocks fell harder than the coin. The 30-day BTC–Nasdaq correlation is 0.67, so US equities around Nvidia's results will pass straight through to BTC; the cycle read is unchanged.

news.title: Nvidia reports after the US close on Nov 17, its first report since the co-founder stepped down as CEO; consensus EPS is $2.47
news.read: Options already price these days: 7-day implied vol is 44.2%, 3.7 points above 90 days. A beat or a miss both widen the swing; we take no view on direction.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost about $1.07B net over Nov 9–13 and about $2.35B over two weeks; IBIT is on 11 straight days of outflows
news.read: On our CoinMarketCap basis Nov 9–13 totals −$883M and 20 days −$2.08B; the methods differ but the direction matches. The estimated ETF holder cost sits above the close, so most of the selling is at a loss.

news.title: Market-wide liquidations topped $2B in 24 hours on Sunday; stablecoin supply shrank $14–16B in a month
news.read: Our stablecoin 30-day change is −$15.6B (DefiLlama), consistent with theirs. After the liquidations, funding went from 1% back to 6.5% in a day: the flushed longs came right back.

news.title: US October PPI rose 0.3% m/m (1.4% in September) and 6.5% y/y; core rose 0.5% m/m
news.read: Monthly growth slowed but the yearly rate is still high, and hike pricing has not eased: Polymarket gives a December hike 96%, and the 2-year yield is 0.83 points above the top of the fed funds range. A tight money backdrop; the cycle read is unchanged.

news.title: Bank of Russia retail crypto rules take effect Nov 17: non-qualified investors may buy BTC, ETH and USDT, with an annual cap per intermediary
news.read: A new compliant buying channel over the long run, but capped, so the near-term volume is small; exchanges can start trading from Nov 22 at the earliest. No immediate effect on our flow numbers.

findings.title: 390K BTC changed hands at a loss into 64–65K, resetting short-term cost
findings.lean_why: Loss sellers were replaced by new buyers whose cost sits near the current price, which lightens the next wave of selling; but loss-taking has not faded, and short-term supply below 62K is thin.
findings.what: Is 64–66K support now, or the next batch of sellers? So far it looks like a repricing: about 390K BTC moved at a loss this week, mostly landing in the 64K and 65K buckets, and the thickest short-term holder layer at 64–66K holds 644K BTC (Bitview, Nov 16).
findings.why: Split the two sides. Short-term holders hold 3.80M BTC at a 73,578 cost, and 74% is now underwater; this week URPD lost 60–140K BTC in each of the 75K, 74K and 77K buckets, while the 64K and 65K buckets gained 207K and 129K BTC (Bitview). The behavior is loss selling: STH-SOPR at 0.963 is the lowest in 282 days, with 10,793 BTC of realized loss against 2,107 BTC of profit, versus 3,931 BTC of loss a week ago (CheckOnChain). Long-term holders did not widen their selling: their 7-day realized loss is $2.05B, slightly below yesterday's $2.09B. Over 30 days, an estimated 1.22M BTC of short-term supply moved and 1.63M BTC arrived.
findings.alt: URPD moves are not necessarily trades; exchange wallet reshuffles also reprice coins, and this week's split has no entity adjustment. The 30-day turnover is an estimate, 2.0% off the actual figure. CheckOnChain's short-term holder P&L is smoothed and about a day late.
findings.history: Concentrated short-term loss-taking with the close below the 200-day average has happened 23 times since 2012; 30 days later price was higher 10 times, median −0.8%, about the same as any day. The last time STH-SOPR was this low was Feb 7, 2026 at 0.958, two days after the Feb 5 low at 62,858.
findings.so: What changed is the next set of sellers: most of the high-priced short-term supply has already been handed over at a loss, and the new holders' cost sits at 64–65K, so a break below would quickly turn them into loss sellers. What did not change is today's hedge.
findings.next: By Nov 20: loss-taking strength under 2 with closes above 63K means the turnover is done and 64–66K turns into support; a close below 62,000 means this new batch of buyers is capitulating too.

findings.title: Funding bounced from 1% to 6.5% in a day as longs paid their way back in
findings.lean_why: After a 25% drop, leveraged longs are still adding, and the long-account share is in the top 4% since 2021; past crowding like this was usually followed by lower prices 90 days later.
findings.what: The weekend liquidations did not wash out the longs: weighted funding went from 0.96% back to 6.51%, and 75.3% of Binance accounts are long, the 96th percentile since 2021 (Coinalyze, Nov 16).
findings.why: Based on deriv.funding_multi, ls_acct and taker; no signal listed it. Every venue flipped positive: Binance 6.8%, Bybit 5.5%, OKX 4.9%, Hyperliquid 10.1%. At the same time perps saw 81K BTC of net taker selling over 7 days and open interest fell 5.9% in a week, so some traders are cutting while others pay up to go long; longs held by Hyperliquid's top 2,000 accounts rose from 7,965 to 8,475 BTC in a day. Spot shows no matching demand, with Coinbase at 9,765 BTC of net taker selling over 7 days.
findings.alt: The funding rebound could also be a mechanical effect of short covering, or spot-perp arbitrage positions; the account share counts accounts, not position size. Hyperliquid is a single venue, and large accounts may be market making or hedging.
findings.history: In the 26 stretches of a high Binance long-account share, price was higher 90 days later 10 times, median −7.0% (any day: up 53%, +2.0%); the latest, on Jun 25, 2026 at 59,772, was followed by +41% over 90 days, and that one was also near a low.
findings.so: What changed is yesterday's "funding reset" read: the reset lasted one day and the direction of leverage did not change. What did not change is the plan's action or the cycle stage.
findings.next: By Nov 20: weighted funding above 8% with long accounts still above 75% means longs are adding; funding back under 2% means the bounce was just short covering.

research.summary: Glassnode's Nov 16 Market Pulse matches our readings: short-term holders are at a loss on average, realized P&L is the worst since July, and leverage was flushed over the weekend; it puts 25-delta skew at its highest since August, while our 25-delta risk reversal has already recovered from −11 to −5.2.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week and briefly broke 63K; futures open interest is $34.2B, the lowest since August; 25-delta skew is 13.7%, the highest since August; weekly ETF outflows of $995M with ETF MVRV at 1.06, near break-even; short-term holder NUPL is −7.4% and the realized P&L ratio is the lowest since early July; it concludes leverage was flushed and the market is less crowded.
items.meaning: "Less crowded" held for one day: our weighted funding was back from 0.96% to 6.51% on Nov 16, with 75% of accounts long (see 2026-11-16-2).

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below short-term holder cost of 75.6K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price, and the only thick layer below is 62–66K; stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days; the largest long liquidation band is 59.5–62.6K; holding the June low at 58.5K keeps August's trend reversal intact.
items.meaning: The 62–66K layer it named is exactly where the most coins changed hands this week (see 2026-11-16-1); its 58.5K is the same low as Tidemark's 58,525 test line.

items.title: Bitcoin: Correction or Reset?
items.points: As reported in the media: reclaiming short-term holder cost with 3 straight days of ETF inflows marks a correction; otherwise it is a reset.
items.meaning: We did not read the original, so it does not drive our view; by its split, a close 12.8% below short-term holder cost of 74,301 with 7 straight days of ETF outflows is still on the reset side.
